summary: Independent full chronology review of the sealed mingshi/034 job: all 22 owned Chinese units, all seven temporal/hint items and both people checked. No repair memo, proposal or other worker judgment was consulted. The first Yuan Zhiyuan reign, Wang's year-17 calendar completion, competing year-18/year-19 death traditions, and Guo's post-death compilation by year-23 presentation are independently supported by checked primary passages and Academia Sinica calendar queries. Bounded uncertainty is valid, not an unresolved conversion: preserve AD 1281-1283 for Wang's death and AD 1281-1287 for Guo's compilation without selecting point years. No locally stated birth, age or death is omitted. Units s0001-s0010 and s0016-s0022 contain headings, calendrical methods and table-omission notices, not further personal chronology; s0014 is later bibliographical attribution, not Wang's activity. Approval concerns only the entire supplied Chinese source: s0017 and s0022 explicitly omit tables, whose absent contents are not certified. The original Chinese Notes URL currently returns 404; the sealed Chinese, not a replacement web transcription, remains the reviewed chapter. Twelve independently checked, hash-pinned external excerpts document the research.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xun's own death, retained as an uncertain death attestation rather than an activity span.
itemChecks.reason: s0012 explicitly dates Wang's death to nineteen, inheriting s0011's reign context. Yuan shi 52 and 164 establish Yuan Shizu's Zhiyuan, not the sealed source's Zhizheng. Yuan shi 164's Guo biography and Yuan mingchen shilue 9's Guo entry both transmit nineteen; the latter work's Wang opening summary transmits sixteen, next-year completion, next-year death, hence eighteen. Wang's Yuan shi biography has year-18 mourning followed by 未幾卒, which does not independently force an exact year. The candidate preserves these witnesses and its regnalYear:19 records the local numeral, not a selected historical solution, as the annotation and uncertain certainty expressly explain. The independently queried first days of Zhiyuan 18 and 20 fall in AD 1281 and 1283 respectively, so inclusive year bounds 1281-1283 safely enclose both alternatives, including a possible early-1283 tail of year 19. No third death tradition, exact Gregorian day, or continuous activity is asserted.

evidence.quote: 按《元史》，至正十七年《授時曆》成。
十九年王恂卒，時歷雖頒，然立成之數尚皆有定藁。

itemChecks.event: Wang Xun's participation in completion of the Shoushi calendar in Yuan Shizu's Zhiyuan 17.
itemChecks.reason: s0011 states calendar completion and retains the problematic 至正 reading; s0012 and s0014-s0015 connect Wang to the calendrical work, without themselves explicitly listing him as a year-17 participant. Targeted corroboration is therefore necessary and is supplied by Wang's own Yuan shi 164 biography and the named reform team in Yuan shi 52. Both place completion in year 17; volume 52 specifies winter solstice. Their ruler and reign context identifies the original Zhiyuan of Shizu, excluding both Zhizheng and the later reused Zhiyuan. Academia Sinica returns the first day of Shizu Zhiyuan 17 in AD 1280, independently confirming the conventional label. The candidate explicitly retains source wording and explains the correction; it does not convert a lunar month/day to Gregorian or date the later two-fascicle compilation to 1280. Different promulgation wording in the two external passages does not contradict their common completion year.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xun's explicitly narrated death, not Guo's subsequent work or a later attribution.
itemChecks.reason: The death predicate correctly owns 王恂卒 in s0012 and agrees with claim-3. The chapter's nineteen is preserved verbatim as its source numeral while the annotated dateContext acknowledges competing Zhiyuan eighteen/nineteen witnesses. Independently read Yuan mingchen shilue 9 and Yuan shi 164 substantiate that conflict. The lower AD 1281 bound is the Western year containing the beginning of Zhiyuan 18; the upper AD 1283 bound admits the final part of Zhiyuan 19 before the checked beginning of year 20 in early 1283. These are inclusive bounds for one death, not a three-year lifespan or a decision between witnesses. Neither an exact death day nor an age-derived birth year is invented. The external age forty-seven is not stated in any owned local unit and does not require expansion of this targeted chapter audit.

itemChecks.event: Guo Shoujing's arrangement of the ready reckoners into two fascicles after Wang's death and by presentation.
itemChecks.reason: The subject of s0013 is Guo, and its narrative follows Wang's death in s0012. s0015 distinguishes Wang's prior draft from Guo's completion without giving a completion year. The checked Guo passages in Yuan shi 164 and Yuan mingchen shilue 9 specifically include 立成二卷 among the works subsequently presented in Zhiyuan 23. Thus presentation supplies a terminus ante quem, not an exact compilation year; Guo's event must not inherit 1280 from the earlier Shoushi calendar completion. The candidate's lower bound AD 1281 accommodates the earliest retained Wang death witness, year 18, and same-year sequence is possible. The checked start of Zhiyuan 24 is in January AD 1287, so undated presentation during year 23 may be in early 1287. The inclusive upper 1287 bound is justified rather than a false exact 1286 completion. SourceDate's annotation is explanatory synthesis, not a purported continuous verbatim chapter quotation.

itemChecks.event: Guo Shoujing's scholarly role as compiler who arranged and reduced the work to two fascicles.
itemChecks.reason: The action, role and person agree directly with s0013. The explicit certainty describes an explicitly narrated action; its dateContext expressly bounds the uncertain date rather than claiming a precise completion year. This context matches claim-17: Wang's death precedes the compilation, while the independently checked Guo accounts give presentation of the two-fascicle ready reckoners in Zhiyuan 23. The earliest retained death tradition yields the inclusive lower Western-year bound 1281; the verified year-23/year-24 boundary yields upper bound 1287. There is no transfer of Wang's death to Guo or of the later edition's date to either person's life. The chapter's speculative s0015 authorship explanation is not needed to make Guo's preceding explicit compilation sentence factual, and its uncertainty is not silently resolved into a precise date.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xun's supported calendar-completion date and expressly uncertain death chronology.
itemChecks.reason: The two hints completely summarize the supplied Wang temporal items without treating him as active throughout a window. AD 1280 is the independently verified conventional Shizu Zhiyuan-17 calendar-completion label, while the death hint explicitly preserves both year-18/year-19 traditions and inclusive bounds AD 1281-1283 established by calendar boundaries. A death may appropriately appear as a labeled terminal identity-date hint; it is not being asserted as continuing activity after death. s0014's 今欽天監本 is later bibliographical reception, excluded from Wang's life dates. s0015 conjectures a prior draft but supplies no additional securely dated event. All remaining units were checked and contain no locally stated Wang birth, age or further death date requiring another hint.

itemChecks.reason: The hint matches both Guo temporal claims and makes clear that the exact completion year is unstated. Its lower AD 1281 and upper AD 1287 bounds follow from the independently checked competing Wang death witnesses, the Guo year-23 presentation passage, and Shizu Zhiyuan calendar boundaries. The wording describes uncertainty about one personal compilation event, not activity throughout 1281-1287, not Wang's death as Guo's life event, and not an exact year-23 compilation. The chapter's earlier calendar-completion statement does not locally date a separate Guo event requiring expansion, and supplementary research need not import his entire biography. The full local text has no Guo birth, age or death to add; 卒成 in s0015 means ultimately completed, not Guo died.

The chapter explicitly states Wang's death, which is captured consistently in claim-3, claim-5 and hints; it states no birth or age. Calendar completion is separately assigned to him with checked primary corroboration, not mistaken for Guo's later compilation. The retained year-18/year-19 conflict is real and bounded correctly, without resolving it from an externally stated inclusive age or inventing a birth year. The source's erroneous 至正 is transparently preserved and its historical interpretation verified as Shizu's first Zhiyuan. The current Astronomical Bureau edition's credit in s0014 is posthumous attribution rather than renewed activity; s0015's prior-draft suggestion has no missing absolute date. The omitted astronomical tables in s0017/s0022 are not reviewed contents, and no completeness claim is made for them. Within the entire supplied source, there is no omitted locally stated life chronology or contradiction.

references.title: Yuan shi 52: Shoushi calendar under Yuan Shizu
references.quote: 十七年冬至，曆成，詔賜名曰授時曆。十八年，頒行天下。
references.reason: The preceding 至元四年 and 世祖 identify the first Yuan Zhiyuan reign. The named team includes Wang Xun and Guo Shoujing. This confirms calendar completion at the winter solstice of year 17 and promulgation in year 18, rather than the local 至正 reading or completion of Guo's later ready reckoners.

references.title: Yuan shi 164: Wang Xun calendar completion
references.quote: 十七年，曆成，賜名授時曆，以其年冬，頒行天下。
references.reason: Wang's own biography independently identifies his participation in the calendar completed in year 17. Its promulgation wording differs from the calendrical treatise but both agree on completion in year 17; the candidate does not equate that event with the later two-fascicle compilation.

references.title: Yuan shi 164: Wang Xun mourning and death
references.quote: 十八年，居父喪，哀毀，日飲勺水。帝遣內侍慰諭之。未幾，卒，年四十七。
references.reason: This places Wang's death shortly after the year-18 mourning narrative, without an express death-year numeral. It supports the earlier tradition but cannot alone force death into year 18. The externally stated age is not a locally omitted age and is not used to infer a precise birth year.

references.title: Yuan shi 164: Guo Shoujing compilation and presentation
references.quote: 十九年，恂卒。時曆雖頒，然其推步之式，與夫立成之數，尚皆未有定藁。守敬於是比次篇類，整齊分杪，裁為推步七卷，立成二卷，曆議擬藁三卷，轉神選擇二卷，上中下三曆注式十二卷。二十三年，繼為太史令，遂上表奏進。
references.reason: Guo's biography expressly gives death in year 19, followed by Guo's compilation including two fascicles of ready reckoners and presentation in year 23. Presentation is an upper deadline, not a stated compilation year. The witness has 未有定藁 whereas sealed s0012 has 有定藁; neither transcription is silently substituted for the other.

references.title: Yuan mingchen shilue 9: Wang Xun opening chronology
references.quote: 十六年拜太史令明年厯成又明年卒年四十七
references.reason: Su Tianjue's Wang entry gives the sequence year 16 appointment, following year completion, and following year death: a distinct year-18 death witness. This is an opening summary, not the Siku general preface. The following mourning narrative is headed 十八年. Preserve its conflict with Guo's year-19 witness without voting for a single year.

references.title: Yuan mingchen shilue 9: Guo compilation tradition
references.quote: 十九年太史王公卒時厯雖頒然其推步之式與夫立成之數尚皆未有定槀公於是比次篇數整齊分秒裁為推步七卷立成二卷厯擬槀三卷轉神選擇二卷上中下三厯注式十二卷二十三年繼為太史令遂上表奏進
references.reason: The Guo entry, attributed to an account of conduct, already preserves year 19 death and year 23 presentation. The conflict therefore occurs within the earlier compilation as well as Yuan shi. These related witnesses are not counted as independent votes; they establish competing transmitted traditions and the presentation deadline.
